conceptZh: 玩具機器人打開一個玩具箱，積木像瀑布一樣噴出來把他整個埋住，只剩一隻手伸在外面比讚；接著積木自己排好：左邊三橫一豎成「王」，右邊兩橫加兩隻小腳成「元」，合成「玩」。
object: a small toy robot, a toy chest and a flood of chunky plastic bricks
morph: the spilled bricks arrange into three bars crossed by one upright for the left 王 and two bars over two short legs for the right 元, forming 玩
creativeAngle: 直接對上樂高積木：笑點是「開箱被自己的玩具埋掉，還從積木堆裡伸出一隻手比讚」，而被倒出來的積木正好是組字的材料，笑點與變形是同一件事。玩只有八畫、左右結構乾淨，適合做完整組裝。語音詞「玩具」，兩字都是單一讀音。
promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second 3D stylized toy animation as one continuous locked-off shot on a clean solid pale sky background. Centered, a small boxy toy robot heaves open the lid of a chunky toy chest with great anticipation. At 1.0 second the chest erupts: a waterfall of colourful plastic bricks pours out and buries him completely in a neat heap. Silence. At 2.0 seconds one small hand pushes up out of the pile and gives a steady thumbs-up. Hold that beat. At 2.6 seconds the heap sorts itself out: three long flat bricks settle on the left as three evenly spaced horizontal bars with one upright brick clicking down through their centres, while on the right two shorter bars stack above two little standing bricks that form a pair of legs. The robot pops his head out at the top, nods at his work, and hops out of frame to the left by 4.4 seconds. By 4.8 seconds the build has resolved into one correctly formed Traditional Chinese character 玩 in saturated deep grape purple, perfectly centered and uncropped, filling about 70% of the frame height with generous margins, its left 王 and right 元 clearly separated and every stroke crisp. From 4.9 to 8.0 seconds the frame holds completely still on 玩 with nothing else moving in the shot. Style: Pixar-like glossy chunky toy materials, soft studio lighting, bright high-contrast colors that are vivid but never neon, no dark or moody grading, no white blowouts. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin and says exactly 「玩、玩、玩具」, using the reading ㄨㄢˊ for 玩 both on its own and inside the word. Speak the first 玩 around 0.5 seconds, the second around 2.0 seconds, and 玩具 around 5.6 seconds while the finished glyph is held still, with natural pauses, then stop; do not keep chanting the character or repeat the line. Keep every sound effect soft and clear of the voice, and use no music louder than the voice. The spoken word is audio only and must not be added to the picture. The only writing anywhere in the frame is the single character 玩: no subtitles, no vocabulary text, no other letters, numbers, watermarks, scenery, extra props, particles, lens flare, motion blur on the glyph, or flashing effects.

conceptZh: 把「玩」變成小怪獸的彈跳遊樂場：得意起跳，撞扁成毛絨餅，再彈回扭蛋裡。
object: An original round fuzzy pocket creature toy, one hinged gachapon capsule, and a solid purple 玩 playground sculpture.
morph: The correctly formed glyph stays intact throughout. The curved foot of 元 becomes a launch perch, and the upright of 王 becomes a rebound surface; only the fuzzy creature squashes and stretches.
creativeAngle: 捨棄積木自動排字，直接讓完整的「玩」示範玩耍。小怪獸把「元」的彎鉤當跳台，卻撞上「王」的直豎，壓成毛絨餅後彈回扭蛋；字形全程不變，笑點來自角色過度自信的彈跳。
promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second stylized 3D toy animation in one locked, front-facing shot. A single correctly formed Traditional Chinese glyph 玩 stands centered against a pale butter-yellow studio background, uncropped and filling about 70% of frame height with generous margins. Use saturated solid plum-purple strokes with shallow rounded depth and a crisp, conventional printed silhouette: a narrow 王 on the left and 元 on the right, including its distinct left-falling stroke and curved hooked right stroke. Preserve every stroke and the spacing throughout. The glyph is a rigid miniature playground, never a deforming character.

The lead is an original round fuzzy turquoise pocket creature toy with tiny feet, expressive eyebrows, and wildly overconfident enthusiasm. Its only supporting prop is one small, unmarked hinged gachapon capsule in the lower-right margin. At 0.0–0.8 seconds, the capsule opens with a gentle pop and the creature springs out, bouncing onto the upward-curving foot of 元. It proudly balances there, eyes fixed on 王, then crouches much too deeply for such a short jump. At 1.6–2.7 seconds, it launches left through the open space beneath the horizontal strokes and meets the lower section of 王’s upright. Its fluffy body compresses into a ridiculous little pancake against the rigid purple surface; its surprised eyes blink once. Keep the contact brief and the glyph intact. At 2.7–3.6 seconds, its fluff springs back, sending it in one clear reverse arc toward the open capsule. Seeing its destination, it changes surprise into a delighted diving pose and lands neatly inside. The lid gently flips shut with a tiny tuft caught outside. The tuft slips in, and the capsule gives one satisfied wiggle before rolling out through the lower-right edge. Finish all action by 4.6 seconds. Hold the complete, unobstructed 玩 absolutely still from 4.6 to 8.0 seconds.

Use soft studio lighting, tactile toy materials, bright restrained colors, and gentle squash-and-stretch confined to the creature. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, saying exactly 「玩、玩、玩具」. Pronounce 玩 as ㄨㄢˊ, first around 0.6 seconds and again around 1.9 seconds, with a natural pause; say 玩具 around 5.5 seconds while the finished glyph is clearly held. Stop after that word. Add only quiet capsule clicks and a soft springy contact sound beneath the voice; no music is needed. The single 玩 is the only visible writing. Keep the vocabulary audio-only, with no subtitles, extra glyphs, logos, watermarks, clutter, or flashing effects.
